propositions: test_contended_index_lock_cleared_during_backoff_succeeds uses a wall-clock threading.Timer to delete a planted index.lock, but the timer can fire after git.commit creates its own real index.lock, causing the timer to delete git's lock mid-commit and fail with 'fatal: unable to write new index file'

on slower runners like macOS py3.13, git commit takes longer than 0.4 seconds, pushing the timer firing into the middle of the commit operation, while faster Linux runners complete before the timer fires
the timer body lacks identity checks to distinguish the test's planted lock from git's real lock, so it unconditionally deletes whatever index.lock exists at t=0.4

the test must be changed to use gitutil._retry_probe (a deterministic probe-based mechanism) instead of threading.Timer, so the planted lock is released only after the first retry attempt, never deleting a lock held by the code under test
